classification.difficultyReason: Recognise the triangular face in both a net and a solid, halve its base, and subtract squared lengths to obtain its altitude rather than using the side edge as the slant height.

content.prompt: You are given a side edge. Calculate the slant height using Pythagoras’ Theorem.

spec.description: Unshaded square-pyramid net with a central square and four attached triangular faces. The base label points to the central square; 45 cm labels a lateral edge of an attached triangle.
spec.mathematics: Square base side 11 cm; triangular face has equal side edges 45 cm. Its slant height bisects the 11 cm base.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied measurements are visible; calculated slant height is withheld.

answer.worked:
The slant height bisects the base of a triangular face.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{11}{2}&=5.5\\l^2+5.5^2&=45^2\\l^2&=2025-30.25\\l^2&=1994.75\\l&=\sqrt{1994.75}\ \mathrm{cm}\end{align*}$$
